review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

14:1.sourceText: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας. καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν.
14:1.targetText: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.

groups.note: μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας ("after two days") is rendered two days away.
πῶς ("how") is rendered a ... way.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").
ἐν δόλῳ ("by stealth") is rendered covert.
The participle κρατήσαντες ("having seized") is rendered as an infinitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle κρατήσαντες is rendered as the infinitive to arrest.
English repeats the object for kill; in Greek αὐτόν serves both verbs.

14:2.sourceText: ἔλεγον γάρ Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, μή ποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ.
14:2.targetText: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”

groups.note: BSB renders the connective γάρ ("for") as But: the Greek explains the covert plan of v. 1, while the English contrasts with it.
μή ποτε ("lest") is rendered or.
The genitive τοῦ λαοῦ ("of the people") is rendered among the people.

14:3.sourceText: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ, κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς· συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς.
14:3.targetText: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ὄντος αὐτοῦ supplies the While-clause.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he").
The participle ἔχουσα ("having") is rendered with.
The genitive νάρδου ("of nard") is rendered made of nard.
κατέχεεν with the genitive means "poured down on".
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The second αὐτοῦ ("he") is not repeated; Jesus is already the subject of the While-clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle συντρίψασα is rendered as the finite verb broke open.
English supplies an object for poured; the Greek has none.

14:4.sourceText: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν;
14:4.targetText: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?

groups.note: ἦσαν ("there were") is rendered by those present.
Εἰς τί ("for what") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves γέγονεν ("has taken place") unexpressed in the short question.

14:5.sourceText: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς· καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ.
14:5.targetText: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.

groups.note: BSB renders τοῦτο τὸ μύρον ("this perfume") as It.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ (for) untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject of given; the Greek says only "and be given to the poor".

14:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἄφετε αὐτήν· τί αὐτῇ κόπους παρέχετε; καλὸν ἔργον ἠργάσατο ἐν ἐμοί.
14:6.targetText: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

groups.note: ἀφίημι means "let go", "leave alone".
κόπους παρέχετε ("do you cause troubles") is rendered are you bothering.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:7.sourceText: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε.
14:7.targetText: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.

groups.note: The present ἔχετε ("you have") is rendered with will.
εὖ ποιῆσαι ("to do good") is rendered help.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ (for) untranslated.

14:8.sourceText: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν· προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν.
14:8.targetText: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.

groups.note: ὃ ἔσχεν ("what she had") is rendered what she could.
προέλαβεν ("she undertook beforehand") is rendered in advance.
εἰς ("for") is rendered of in the phrase in advance of.
The article τόν is rendered as the possessive My.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:9.sourceText: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
14:9.targetText: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

groups.note: ὅπου ἐάν ("where ever") is rendered wherever.

14:10.sourceText: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ, ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς.
14:10.targetText: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:11.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι. καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ.
14:11.targetText: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money.  So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

groups.note: In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
The imperfect ἐζήτει ("he kept seeking") is rendered began to look for.
πῶς ... εὐκαίρως ("how ... conveniently") is rendered an opportunity.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for hear; the Greek has none.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐζήτει.

14:12.sourceText: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων, ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον, λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;
14:12.targetText: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

groups.note: τὸ πάσχα here is the Passover lamb that was sacrificed.
The impersonal ἔθυον ("they used to sacrifice") is rendered as a passive.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the participle ἀπελθόντες ("going") unexpressed.

14:13.sourceText: καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ,
14:13.targetText: So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him,

14:14.sourceText: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ Διδάσκαλος λέγει Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου, ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
14:14.targetText: and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’

groups.note: ὅπου ἐάν ("wherever") is rendered whichever house.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the quotation is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:15.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἕτοιμον· καὶ ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν.
14:15.targetText: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins furnished and ready; the Greek sets the two words side by side.

14:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
14:16.targetText: So the disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover.

groups.note: BSB turns "and they found" into a relative clause about the city.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for found; the Greek has none.
English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.

14:17.sourceText: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
14:17.targetText: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.

groups.note: The genitive absolute participle γενομένης supplies the When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἔρχεται.

14:18.sourceText: καὶ ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με, ὁ ἐσθίων μετ’ ἐμοῦ.
14:18.targetText: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν supplies the while-clause.
The article ὁ with the participle ἐσθίων forms the relative clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.

14:19.sourceText: ἤρξαντο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς κατὰ εἷς Μήτι ἐγώ;
14:19.targetText: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”

groups.note: Μήτι expects the answer no.

14:20.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ ἐμβαπτόμενος μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὸ τρύβλιον.
14:20.targetText: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
The article ὁ with the participle ἐμβαπτόμενος means "the one dipping".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame with no Greek counterpart.
English supplies what is dipped; the Greek says only "the one dipping with me into the bowl".

14:21.sourceText: ὅτι ὁ μὲν Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ· οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
14:21.targetText: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

groups.note: BSB renders ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ("the Son of Man") as He.
BSB renders ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ("that man") as he.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective ὅτι ("for") untranslated.
The particle μέν, answered by δέ (but), has no separate English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek says only καλὸν αὐτῷ ("good for him").

14:22.sourceText: Καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν Λάβετε· τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
14:22.targetText: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν supplies the While-clause.
BSB names the disciples for αὐτοῖς ("to them").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB turns καὶ εἶπεν ("and said") into the participle saying, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle λαβών.
English coordinator; the participle εὐλογήσας is rendered as the finite verb spoke.
English supplies an object for broke; the Greek has none.
English supplies an object for gave; the Greek has none.
English supplies an object for Take; the Greek has none.

14:23.sourceText: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπιον ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες.
14:23.targetText: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participles are rendered as finite verbs joined to gave.
English supplies an object for gave; the Greek has none.

14:24.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν.
14:24.targetText: He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

groups.note: The article τό with the participle ἐκχυννόμενον forms the relative clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:25.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἐκ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:25.targetText: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”

groups.note: οὐκέτι οὐ μή ("no longer, by no means") is an emphatic negative.
The aorist subjunctive under οὐ μή is rendered as an English future.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:26.sourceText: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
14:26.targetText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

targetPhrases.text: when they had sung a hymn

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:27.sourceText: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πάντες σκανδαλισθήσεσθε, ὅτι γέγραπται Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα διασκορπισθήσονται.
14:27.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written:  ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.

14:28.sourceText: ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
14:28.targetText: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

groups.note: μετὰ τό with the infinitive means "after".
με is the subject of the infinitive ἐγερθῆναι.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:29.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη αὐτῷ Εἰ καὶ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγώ.
14:29.targetText: Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”

groups.note: BSB renders οὐκ ("not") as never.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτῷ (to him).
BSB leaves ἀλλά ("yet") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats only the auxiliary of the verb; the Greek is elliptical ("yet not I").

14:30.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι σὺ σήμερον ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ.
14:30.targetText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”

groups.note: σήμερον ("today") is rendered by the emphasis this very night.
πρὶν ἤ means "before".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτῷ (to him).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ὅτι, which introduces the quoted statement.

14:31.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει Ἐὰν δέῃ με συναποθανεῖν σοι, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι. ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ πάντες ἔλεγον.
14:31.targetText: But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Peter.
ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει ("kept saying emphatically") is rendered kept insisting.
με is the subject of the infinitive συναποθανεῖν.
οὐ μή is the emphatic double negative.
The future under οὐ μή is rendered as an English future.
ὡσαύτως ("likewise") is rendered the same thing.
καὶ πάντες ("all also") is rendered all the others.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds emphasis; the Greek has only ἐάν ("if").

14:32.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς χωρίον οὗ τὸ ὄνομα Γεθσημανεί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Καθίσατε ὧδε ἕως προσεύξωμαι.
14:32.targetText: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

groups.note: οὗ τὸ ὄνομα ("whose name was") is rendered called.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

14:33.sourceText: καὶ παραλαμβάνει τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάνην μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤρξατο ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν,
14:33.targetText: He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί between the first two names is represented by a comma in BSB's list.

14:34.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε.
14:34.targetText: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:35.sourceText: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπιπτεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ προσηύχετο ἵνα εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρέλθῃ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα,

groups.note: μικρόν ("a short distance") is rendered a little farther.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

14:36.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ, πάντα δυνατά σοι· παρένεγκε τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· ἀλλ’ οὐ τί ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλὰ τί σύ.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has no verb here.

14:37.sourceText: καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ Σίμων, καθεύδεις; οὐκ ἴσχυσας μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι;

14:39.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών.

14:40.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν ἐλθὼν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καταβαρυνόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τί ἀποκριθῶσιν αὐτῷ.
